2607.17783.title: Feature Attribution-Based Explainability Analysis of Deep Learning Models in Predictive Process Monitoring
2607.17783.paper_summary: Predictive process monitoring supports the optimization and control of operational business processes by forecasting the future state or outcome of ongoing cases. While deep neural networks have achieved strong performance for these tasks by modeling sequential dependencies in event logs, their black-box nature limits trust and practical adoption. Feature attribution methods are often used to address this, but applying them directly poses a dilemma: event-level attributions impose high computational complexity for long traces, while explanations based on aggregated trace representations often fail to capture the underlying control-flow dynamics. To address this issue, we propose a local post-hoc explainability method for deep neural networks in outcome prediction. The method relies on a control-flow-aware segmentation algorithm that partitions a trace into meaningful segments and supports the computation of segment-level SHAP explanations. This makes it possible to identify which parts of a trace influence a prediction and which change points steer the case toward the predicted outcome. We assess the proposed segmentation method on a synthetic dataset with known process logic, where meaningful change points can be explicitly verified, and we demonstrate its usefulness on real-world event logs from a loan application process and an administrative process of a Dutch municipality.
2607.17783.paper_summary_zh: 預測過程監控透過預測正在進行的案例的未來狀態或結果，支持操作業務流程的優化和控制。雖然深度神經網絡在這些任務中通過建模事件日誌中的序列依賴性已經取得了良好的表現，但其黑箱特性限制了信任和實際採用。特徵歸因方法通常用於解決這個問題，但直接應用它們會帶來兩難：事件級別的歸因對於長追蹤會帶來高計算複雜度，而基於聚合追蹤表示的解釋往往無法捕捉到潛在的控制流程動態。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了一種針對深度神經網絡在結果預測中的局部事後可解釋性方法。該方法依賴於一種控制流程感知的分段算法，將追蹤劃分為有意義的段並支持計算段級別的SHAP解釋。這使得能夠識別追蹤中哪些部分影響預測，以及哪些變更點將案例引導到預測的結果。我們在一個具有已知過程邏輯的合成數據集上評估所提出的分段方法，在這裡有意義的變更點可以明確驗證，並且我們在來自荷蘭市政府的貸款申請過程和行政過程的真實事件日誌中展示了其實用性。
